newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Croesus doubles Binduli gold estimate.
newsitem.headline: Croesus doubles Binduli gold estimate.

text.p: Gold miner and explorer Croesus Mining NL said on Wednesday it had more than doubled the size of eastern contact mineralisation (ECM) at Binduli near Kalgoorlie in Western Australia and discovered a new gold deposit five kilometres to the north.

In a statement accompanying its June 1997 quarterly report, Croseus said a recent resource estimate on the Centurion deposit had extended the ECM to 119,000 tonnes at 12.3 grams per tonne of gold, increasing the strike length and ore zone thickness of the black shale contact.
"This free milling ore has increased the total Centurion sulphide resource by 38 percent to 146,000 ounces," it said.
Croesus said the Navajo deposit resource had also increased by 22 percent and now totalled 9.6 million tonnes at 1.12 g/t gold or 347,000 contained ounces.

It said drilling at the Fort William deposit, north of Centurion, outlined mineralisation over a strike length of 400 metres and significant results included 47 metres at 3.38 g/t gold, 24 m at 2.93 g/t and 19 m at 2.33 g/t.
Binduli's mineral resource inventory currently stood at 846,000 ounces and was yet to include Fort William, it said.

Croseus managing director Steve Johnston said the company was considering installing a two-stage crushing circuit at Binduli, superceding plans for a A$20 million standalone plant, and to upgrade the grinding circuit at Hannon South.
This would allow the treatment plant to treat primary ore at a rate of 500,000 tonnes per annum and lower primary ore treatment costs, he said.
"If the upgrade proceeds, production of Centurion primary ore would commence as early as the last 1997 quarter," he said.

Johnston said the company had a solid gold forward sale position of 92,500 ounces of gold, approximately two years of production, at an average price of A$611 per ounce, with cash and bullion reserves of A$16 million.
During the quarter, the Binduli mine processed 152,317 tonnes of ore and produced 7,276 ounces of fine gold at a cash cost of A$306 per ounce, the statement said.
